semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer m ≥ 2 and every integer g ≥ 0, there exists a function J_{m,g} mapping each x ∈ K_{m,g} (i.e., each positive integer (m−1)-tuple with sum g and satisfying the given conditional inequalities for all i,j∈{1,...,m−1}) into K_{m,g+1} (same constraints but sum g+1), such that for all x,y ∈ K_{m,g}, x ≠ y implies J_{m,g}(x) ≠ J_{m,g}(y).

shared_context.statement_nl: For every integer m >= 2 and every integer g >= 0, the number N(m, g) of numerical semigroups with multiplicity m and genus g satisfies N(m, g) <= N(m, g + 1).

payload.statement_nl: Let m be an integer with m >= 2 and let g be an integer with g >= 0. Define K_{m,g} to be the set of all tuples x = (x_1,...,x_{m-1}) of positive integers such that for all i,j in {1,...,m-1}, if i + j < m then x_i + x_j >= x_{i+j}, and if i + j > m then x_i + x_j + 1 >= x_{i+j-m}, and such that x_1 + ... + x_{m-1} = g. Define K_{m,g+1} analogously with coordinate sum g+1. Then there exists an injective function J_{m,g} from K_{m,g} to K_{m,g+1}.

result_payload.proof_summary: I could not produce a complete rigorous proof of the stated injective-map lemma from the given self-contained definitions alone. I explored several natural candidates for J_{m,g}, such as increasing a fixed coordinate or increasing a coordinate of minimal value, but none yielded an immediately valid injective construction in full generality.

suspected_gaps: I do not have a general injective construction J_{m,g}.

Several natural constructions fail: increasing a fixed coordinate can violate the defining inequalities; increasing a least-minimal coordinate preserves membership but is not injective (already for m=3, x=(1,2) and x'=(2,1) both map to (2,2) under that rule).
I also do not have a cardinality proof that |K_{m,g}|<=|K_{m,g+1}| for all m,g from the given data.

result_payload.stuck_point: The core difficulty is finding a function J_{m,g}:K_{m,g}->K_{m,g+1} that is simultaneously well-defined and injective for all m and g. A promising observation is that if one increments a coordinate attaining the global minimum value t, then the defining inequalities are preserved, because whenever that coordinate appears on the right-hand side, the left-hand side is at least 2t (or 2t+1), hence at least t+1. However, the obvious deterministic choices of which minimal coordinate to increment are not injective: for m=3, both x=(1,2) and x'=(2,1) lie in K_{3,3}, and incrementing the unique minimal coordinate in each case gives the same image (2,2) in K_{3,4}. I do not see how to modify this into a global injective rule with a rigorous proof.
